
## We are pushing the limits of imaging neural activity with light


* deeper in the brain: three-photon imaging (Cloves + Margrie 2025)
* higher frequency: 
  * voltage imaging
  * various GECI indicators 
* more of the brain: meso-scale imaging
* in a more naturalistic setting: freely moving
* larger volumes: light bead microscopy
* for longer: multiday recordings
* more control: optical stimulation

Analysis tools need to be chosen appropriately.

## Analysis of multiphoton imaging series

* image acquisition ) -> motion correction -> segmentation on a reference image -> fluorescence extraction -> DF/F -> deconvolution ( -> downstream analysis

## Analysis software ecosystem is fragmented, fragile and rigid

Widely adopted tools:
Suite2p: good for cortical two-photon. Most popular. Bugs don't get ans
CaImAn: good for 1-photon (worse SNR)
In practice, both applied to similar experiments.
Many labs also roll their own

Commercial tools (?)

Not interoperable -> hard to benchmark, hard to compare, hard to adapt to new experiments
Need flexibility, guidance, performance, transparency, collaboration

Improving on this needs community buy-in
